rubric.criterion: Fail: The review omits most material consequences, gives fixes that cannot be acted on, or invents defects. Partial: The review identifies some material consequences and actionable fixes but is incomplete or includes an unsupported claim. Pass: Each important finding explains its concrete consequence in this project and gives a fix a developer can act on, without invented problems. (code cannot check this because ...)

findingsKey.finding: rotateRefreshToken appends a replacement record but leaves the record containing the presented refresh token active, so a stolen token can be replayed after a successful rotation.

Refresh-token lookup uses JavaScript string equality even though this credential is attacker-controlled, which exposes a timing signal and bypasses the token service's constant-time comparison helper.
The remember-me cookie options only set Max-Age, so the persistent credential is sent without HttpOnly or Secure and can be read by script or sent over an insecure connection.
Password-reset links now use Math.random for their secret token, making a high-impact account-recovery credential predictable instead of cryptographically random.
Changing the password updates the account but never calls the available session revocation operation, leaving every existing device signed in despite the documented password-change policy.
Logout only emits expired browser cookies and does not revoke the matching server session, so a copied session cookie remains usable after logout.
